Reference

Feature traceability

This page maps every user-visible Ilium feature to its owner after the move to plugins. The ids F-001 to F-111 are the feature numbers of the feature inventory (docs/research/plugin-platform/feature-inventory.md, features 1 to 111). F-112 to F-116 are features the inventory folds into other rows; they get their own rows so each has its own parity test. The "User doc" column names the page in src/docs/ that describes the feature today. The "Kind" column uses the inventory classification: native-kernel, plugin-wasm, primitive-extended and plugin-js. The "Wave" column uses the phases and waves of the roadmap. The COR ids point to core parity requirements.

[COR-003] Two checks run over this table. A row whose Kind is native-kernel names kernel first in its Owner cell. Every table named in the Config keys column appears in the key-by-key table of config and data migration. [COR-001] Every feature in this table MUST keep working with the same behaviour when its owner plugin is enabled. [COR-002] Every row MUST have one primary owner, the first one named in its Owner cell; later names are supporting owners. A feature that two pages claim is listed once, under "Resolved duplicates".

Related pages: kernel and boot, config and data migration, CLI compatibility, core plugins.

Resolved duplicates

Five features were claimed by two core-plugin pages. Each now has one owner. The other page links to the owner.

Feature Claimed by Owner Reason
Session conversion compaction and session-convert session-convert Compaction only resumes its summary into a new session. Conversion between Claude and Codex is one feature (F-077).
Setup tab and agent setup chatroom and agent-setup agent-setup It writes the agent instruction files for chatroom and progress (F-037, F-063).
Onboarding settings and voice settings The guided setup is one flow (F-089). Voice owns only the demo step (F-053).
new-pane --worktree fleet and worktrees worktrees creates the worktree; fleet owns the command The command parses arguments. The worktree service does the Git work (F-067, F-107).
Plugins screen keys and help keys-and-help and settings settings owns the screen; keys-and-help owns help topics One screen, one owner.

Reconciliation with the feature inventory

  • The inventory has 111 features. This table has 116 rows: the 111 inventory features plus F-112 to F-116, which the inventory folds into other features. No feature is dropped.
  • Feature 108 (ilium wait) is native-kernel in the inventory. The manual makes it an alias of ilium progress wait, so the progress plugin owns it and the Kind is plugin-wasm. The kernel keeps no wait command.
  • Features 19, 20, 21, 24 and 25 (editors and boards) are native-kernel in the inventory. They become plugins in phase 7, so the table names the editor and kanban plugins as the final owners and gives rows owned only by a plugin (F-020, F-021, F-025, F-107) the Kind plugin-wasm (see roadmap).
  • Features 93 and 94 (shared look, dithering and display) stay in the kernel painter. The ambient look plugin owns only the controls.
  • Feature 58 (HTTP API) stays in the kernel as the listener. The fleet plugin registers POST /create_agent through http-api.route.
  • Feature 102 (packaged JavaScript animations) is plugin-js in the inventory. The roadmap retires the V8 runtime at the end of wave 4c. Scenes become wasm packages.
  • Features 72, 77 and 88 have no source path in the inventory; their owners follow the user documentation.
